source.title: Irish News, 3 February 1995, p. 4 ("Leak fiasco lost us crucial votes claim loyalists (all counts)"); News Letter, 3 February 1995, p. 9 ("Vote boost for Molyneaux (Macedon Ward result, electorate, quota, turnout)"); Belfast Telegraph, 2 February 1995, p. 35 ("UU wins by-election (count-day report)"); Belfast Telegraph, 3 February 1995, p. 4 ("Result table (first count; final count; Total votes 3,895; Quota 1,895; turnout 29.5pc)"); Irish News, 3 November 1994, p. 7 ("Ill health results in council vacancy (Blair disqualified)")
source.publisher: Irish News / News Letter / Belfast Telegraph (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: First preferences sum to 3,789; quota floor(3,789/2)+1 = 1,895 = printed, so 3,789 is the valid poll. 3,895 printed as total votes (BT) - Irish News calls it 'valid votes', which the quota contradicts; it matches 29.5% of 13,207 (3,896), so it is the total poll and c. 106 papers were spoilt (not reported). Count 2: Kidd +303 (927), Kirkham +34 (641). Count 3: Robinson 1,525, Kidd 1,076, De Courcy 1,000 (excluded). Count 4: Robinson 2,211 (elected), Kidd 1,251. ARK percentages (UUP 31, DUP 22, Lab 16, UDP 16, Alliance 14) match.

note: By-election of 1 February 1995 for one seat in Macedon (Newtownabbey), caused by the Alliance councillor John (Kenneth) Blair disqualified for three months' unauthorised absence (ill health); seat declared vacant early November 1994; UUP mayor opposed co-option.

countGroup.Party_Basis: Printed 'Lab'; Mark Langhammer's Newtownabbey Labour group, under whose label Kidd sat on the council (ARK, Newtownabbey 1993-2011)
